{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVfxoTs8AAAABiSHohQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bpzn1zhLpfKw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bpzn1", "number": 15, "title": "Publish SFC Studio on GitHub Pages with automated deployment", "body": "## Goal
Integrate an automated GitHub Pages deployment pipeline for the existing SFC Studio browser application, so users can open it without installing Rust or building locally.

## Tasks
- [ ] Inspect existing GitHub Pages settings and deployment workflows; reuse them where appropriate.
- [ ] Add or update a GitHub Actions workflow to build the static site from `tools/studio/web/build.sh` using a reproducible Rust/WASM toolchain, locked dependencies, and wasm-pack.
- [ ] Configure deployment of only the generated `tools/studio/_site/` application and its bundled original demo, not unrelated repository contents, ROMs, private assets, or credentials. Use least-privilege permissions and enable Pages through existing authorized settings/API where permitted.
- [ ] Configure the repository's Pages URL (prefer a stable /studio/ subpath if a site already exists); preserve any existing site. Support repository base paths, relative asset URLs, correct WASM MIME type and HTTPS.
- [ ] Automatically rebuild/deploy on relevant changes to main, with manual workflow dispatch for recovery.
- [ ] Include automated post-deployment HTTP and headless-browser smoke checks for application JS/WASM, demo loading, editing and export.
- [ ] Update the root README and Studio README with the configured URL, deployment instructions and verification procedure. Label live availability as pending until verified; do not require a verified production URL in the pre-merge PR. Preserve existing game content, ROMs and build pipelines.

## Mandatory acceptance criteria for PR approval, merge and Issue closure
All criteria below must be achievable and machine-verifiable before merging, except the merge itself:
- [ ] The build and existing Studio automated checks pass.
- [ ] Validate the deployment workflow configuration, permissions, triggers and artifact allowlist. Confirm the Pages configuration where accessible; document any actual permissions blocker.
- [ ] Test the exact intended static artifact locally under the repository base path, including MIME types, relative URLs, WASM initialization, demo loading, editing and export using automated HTTP/headless-browser checks.
- [ ] The workflow implements automated live verification after deployment and reports success/failure and the verified URL in its Actions run summary.
- [ ] Documentation distinguishes the configured URL from a verified live deployment and does not impose a pre-merge live verification requirement.
- [ ] After normal automated review and required pre-merge checks pass, merge the implementation PR and close this issue through the existing workflow.

**Do not require a successful production deployment, a live HTTPS response, a post-merge Actions run, or any other result obtainable only after merging as a condition of PR approval, merge or closure of this implementation issue.** Do not leave the PR or this issue blocked waiting for such results. No human confirmation is required. Do not bypass repository protections or failing pre-merge checks.

## Post-merge verification (separate from this issue's completion criteria)
The first relevant push to main should trigger the deployment automatically. The workflow then verifies the actual HTTPS site, JS/WASM, demo resources and the browser editing/export workflow; it records the verified URL and Actions run evidence. If deployment or smoke checks fail, diagnose and retry where appropriate, and track any necessary remediation in a separate follow-up task. These results are not prerequisites for merging or closing #15. Do not report live deployment as successful until the checks actually pass.

## Constraints
Use existing authorized repository permissions; do not change repository visibility, expose unrelated content or bypass security policy. If repository-level permissions prevent enabling Pages, document the exact blocker and available automated alternatives. Deployment and documentation only, not new game development.
